subject: PayWise pilot: proposed model roster, locales, and POC milestones
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@paywise.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PayWise pilot: proposed model roster, locales, and POC milestones

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Below is a concise recap and a proposed POC plan so we can align on scope and timelines. Please flag anything that needs to change.

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: Validate an LLM-based assistant to handle customer billing inquiries and transaction reconciliation for US and LATAM customers (EN, ES, PT).
- Success will be measured by intent accuracy, safe output rate, latency, and cost-per-transaction.
- Data: PayWise will share a 3k-message sample (sanitized), and a list of 100 canonical intents/answers.

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks)
1) Models to evaluate (primary + fallback):
   - Primary (fast, lower-cost): Mistral-7B-Instruct (q8_0) — target for short to mid-length prompts and high throughput.
   - Fallback (higher-capacity, better long-context): Llama-2-Chat-13B (q4_k_m) — to handle complex reconciliation threads and longer contexts.
   - Embeddings: Open-source SBERT-lite or a small Mistral embedding variant for semantic search of transaction logs.
2) Locales: English (US), Spanish (Mexico/Colombia), Portuguese (Brazil). We'll run separate eval slices per locale.
3) Acceptance criteria (first pass):
   - Intent classification F1 >= 0.82 across sampled intents (per-locale).
   - Answer correctness (human eval) >= 85% for top-3 answers on reconciliation tasks.
   - Latency targets: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 450ms in Dedicated mode with a 100rps baseline for our sample load.
   - Cost goal: per-transaction infer cost <= target agreed in Week 0 (placeholder in spreadsheet).

Deliverables and owners
- Week 0 (this week): sample dataset + security questionnaire (PayWise). Owner: PayWise (Luis/Samantha).
- Week 1: technical kickoff + sandbox access (Redwood: Ben).
- Week 2: initial model training/tuning and batching configs (Ben/Platform).
- Week 3: evaluation runs, human-in-the-loop labels (PayWise/Redwood).
- Week 4: final acceptance run + retro (all).

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx, redwood-model-comparison.pdf (attached).

Next steps I suggest:
- Samantha/Luis: confirm sample data delivery date and any locale-specific redaction rules by Mon 5/3.
- We’ll schedule a 60-min technical kickoff — Ben will propose slots.

If that all looks right, I’ll turn this into a mutual action plan and push to HubSpot.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the detailed note and file. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing with product and security: 

1) Models: The architecture choices look sensible. Two items: can Redwood guarantee model determinism for the reconciliation flow (same inputs, stable output when pinned)? Also, for Spanish/Portuguese we're particularly sensitive to hallucination on currency formatting and date parsing.

2) Data delivery: We can deliver the 3k sample by Tue 5/4 but it will be redacted for PII. We will also include a small gold set of 200 labeled examples for human-eval.

3) Security: attaching the PayWise_Security_Reqs.docx. Two quick asks:
   - Need confirmation on data retention for inference logs in Redwood Dedicated vs Private.
   - What level of access will Redwood engineers have to our raw logs during the POC?

4) Acceptance criteria: Product proposed tightening intent F1 to >= 0.85 for EN, >= 0.82 for ES/PT. Can Redwood confirm the evaluation harness will produce per-locale metrics?

If you can answer the security + determinism questions, we’ll confirm kickoff once we have the dataset.

Samantha
Head of Product Operations | PayWise

Hi Samantha — quick answers and an expanded evaluation plan from our side.

Determinism and model pinning
- Redwood supports version pinning of model binaries and quantization profiles in the Dedicated offering; that ensures repeatable inference for a pinned config. For true bit-for-bit determinism there are caveats (GPU scheduling, non-deterministic kernels), but for the POC we can pin a model+quant config and run evaluation with fixed seeds to achieve effectively stable outputs for scoring.

Data access and retention
- Dedicated: inference logs (inputs + model outputs) are retained for the POC period by default in an encrypted store. Retention period is configurable — default 90 days. Access: Redwood engineers will only get access to anonymized logs unless you explicitly request debug access; debug access requires NDA/C2 and an access ticket.
- Private (VPC): logs stay in your VPC and Redwood personnel have zero access unless you provision a support tunnel.

Evaluation harness and metrics
- We’ll run an automated eval pipeline that produces per-locale metrics (intent F1, answer-precision, hallucination indicator flagged by heuristics, latency percentiles). Human eval for answer correctness will be tracked in a shared Google Sheet (or Drive doc) that PayWise can own.

Proposed quantitative thresholds (we can adjust):
- Intent F1: EN >= 0.85, ES >= 0.82, PT >= 0.82
- Human-correctness (reconciliation): >= 85% overall
- Latency (Dedicated baseline): p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 450ms
- Embedding recall@5 for transaction search >= 0.88

Technical kickoff agenda (60 min)
- 10m: Introductions + POC goals
- 15m: Data schema & redaction rules (PayWise)
- 15m: Sandbox access & infra plan (Redwood — Ben)
- 15m: Evaluation plan & acceptance gates
- 5m: Next steps & scheduling

Action items (short list)
- Ben: send calendar poll for kickoff (today).
- Karthik: create HubSpot mutual action plan and attach updated spreadsheet.
- PayWise: deliver sanitized dataset + gold labels by Tue 5/4.

If that aligns, Ben will lead the technical setup and I’ll pair with him on the model runs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
